title: Fantastic habit tracker
body: I’m not one to write reviews as I honestly can’t be bothered most of the time unless I’m writing to complain but this app is significantly better than most. It’s minimalistic yet still interactive. I’m not interested in the invasiveness of other habit trackers that seem too overwhelming and bombard you with sometimes unattainable goal suggestions that just seem unrealistic. I seem to lose interest in many of the other habit tracker apps pretty quickly because they all seem to be the same generic dynamic but this one is quite unique and fun. The options to varying notification settings and the different sculptures that you can complete by achieving your goals/habits is a fantastic idea to keep the consumer captivated. I have recommended this app to many of my friends and they find it great. Kudos to the developers.

title: Weird mixture of awesome and terrible
body:
There are some amazing things about this app - the concept of getting to 60 and getting up the levels is really motivating, plus the animations and retro game vibes are awesome. 

But aside from that, the interface is so hard to use that I had to delete the app. I wanted to love it but I can’t stand it. Nothing works conventionally, even ordinary stuff. I can barely figure out how to do anything. I can’t seem to see all my habits at once? The free themes are either gloomy black or obnoxious industrial yellow and you have to pay a crazy amount for other themes. The contrast is so low on those default themes that I can barely see what stuff is. 

This app is a very cool swing at a better habit tracking experience but because the overall usability is terrible, it ends up being a total miss.

title: Extremely well designed app and fun to use but not worth the subscription
body:
I tried out the Habits app by Not Boring and was pleased surprised at how fun it made Habit tracking. The sounds, haptic feedback, and visuals are all well thought out.

The price currently just for Habits is around €18/year. The app currently stores all data locally on the device, and there are no ongoing running costs so I don’t see why there isn‘t a one-time purchase option.

To the apps‘s credit, the free version is generous and there are no ads, but hiding the widgets behind a subscription just seems an unfair move to me.

I won’t be using this app long-term because I don’t find the recurring price to be worth it for what it offers.

title: Warum gibt es ein Zeichen-Limit für die Namen der Routinen?
body:
Mir gefällt das Design der App sehr. Dass man sich einen Berg oÄ aufbaut, indem man seine Routinen „abhakt“ und dazu Vibrations-Feedback, Animationen und Sounds bekommt find ich auch klasse.
Warum aber kann ich meine Routinen nicht so benennen wie ich es will und muss wegen dem Zeichen-Limit von weniger als 30 plötzlich kreative Abkürzungen erfinden?
Auch toll wäre es, wenn man sagen kann, dass man die Routine nicht an bestimmten Wochentagen, sondern zB alle zwei oder mehr Tage erledigen will.

title: Need more magic
body:
Here’s the thing about habit-tracking apps: they all promise to fix your life. Track this, check that, and suddenly—poof—you’re a productivity ninja. 

Habits isn’t just any app, though. It’s clean, user-friendly, and genuinely helpful. But does it have that secret sauce that keeps you coming back, day after day? Well, not quite.

Let me break it down for you.

What Works:

	1.	Simplicity That Doesn’t Insult You
The interface is so intuitive, even your grandmother could use it to crush her knitting goals. No fluff, no fuss. Just pure, clean & fun design that gets out of your way.

	2.	Customizable Goals Without Overthinking
Want to drink more water? Meditate? Remember to floss? This app lets you set your own priorities instead of forcing you into a cookie-cutter system.

	3.	Feedback You Can Actually Use

There’s a small dopamine hit every time you check something off, and honestly, that’s what we’re all chasing, right?

Where It Falls Short

Here’s the kicker: Habits has everything you need—except the thing you actually need. It’s all surface-level. The app doesn’t go deep, and that’s a problem because building habits isn’t just about ticking boxes. It’s about systems.

What Could Be Better: 

	1.	Automate the “Why”
Right now, the app makes you think too hard about why you’re doing what you’re doing. A James Clear-inspired feature could help link new habits to existing ones. Call it a “habit stacker” or something.

	2.	The magic of reps

Habits misses the magic of streaks and reps—the lifeblood of habit-building. A simple feature to track and celebrate consecutive wins would make the app far more addictive. Think glowing chains or a progress bar that resets if you skip a day. 
Momentum matters, and without it, the app feels static, not dynamic.

	3.	Kill the Perfectionism 
Trap Miss a day? The app subtly guilt-trips you. Missing once is fine, twice not so much. The app needs to reinforce resilience, not rigid perfectionism.

Final Verdict

Habits is like the kid in class who always does their homework but never raises their hand. It’s solid, dependable, and you’d probably lend it your notes. But if it really wants to stand out, it needs to embrace the deeper psychology of habit formation.

Until then, it’s a good tool—but not a great one. Use it, enjoy it, but don’t be afraid to break out of it

Rating: 3.9
Clean, useful, but missing the heart of the matter.

title: Not so Boring Habit Tracker
body:
* Aesthetic Appeal: This habit tracker app stands out with its stunning elegance and beautiful design. The user interface is a perfect blend of simplicity and sophistication, making it a pleasure to use. Each element is thoughtfully placed, contributing to a clean and visually appealing interface that users will find delightful.

* Key Strengths:
    * Visually stunning minimalist layout and superb skin/wallpapers.
    * Direct and uncomplicated functionality.
    * Smooth, uncluttered navigation
    * Just like any other Not Boring apps, Crisp music (Chef’s kiss).

* Some Weaknesses and Recommendations:
    * Removing a habit (or Checkmarks) can be a bit tricky. You need to press and hold the key to remove, and it uses the default Apple layout. (This is a minor nitpick, but it would have been better if the removal layout adhered to the theme.)
    * No Apple Watch support. (Integration with wearable devices, like smartwatches in the future maybe?).
    * No (?) cloud support (I bough the Super membership and I use both the iPhone and iPad almost regularly. It seems that I can’t find any cloud support that let’s me sync my progress to my devices.) - Let me know if there is.

* Overall Rating: ★★★★☆ (4/5 stars)

 Should I recommend it? 100% yes.

title: Beautiful, but bad UX
body:
For the most part, I really like this app. There's no ads and the developers don't collect your data. The app is habit tracking in its simplest form. You just open the app and hold the button, no fluff. 

The sounds and haptics are great, giving you a small dose of dopamine every time you check something off. 

I have a handful of issues, though. First is there's a tight character limit on each habit. I found it hard to squeeze some of my habits in.

Second is I don't care for the cryptic messages you get with every check. Wish I could disable those.

Third and most importantly, the user experience is cumbersome. You have to swipe one at a time through every habit. At the end of every day, when I want to restart back at habit one, I have to swipe through 16 habits. That alone is enough for me to not want to use this app anymore.

Then you have the fact that every time you swipe to a different habit, it brings you back to the checkmark screen. So if I want to look at the calendar view for my habits, I have to swipe up twice to get to the calendar, swipe left to go to the next habit, swipe up twice to again get to the calendar, swipe left to go to the next habit, etc...

The worst part about this is, these issues aren't readily apparent from the free version when you only have two habits to look at. 

Finally, this is personal taste, but I don't like a single one of 10 skins you get with premium, which was a bummer.

title: FEATURES TO ENHANCING THE GAME
body:
This habit tracker has a lot of potential to replacing any habit tracker on the AppStore but it still needs some work. I have some suggestions to improve it but it’s up to you guys (the people who use this app) if you want them added or not.

MY SUGGESTIONS:
Seeing one habit at a time is great but swiping the small names of the habits at the top makes navigating to other habits annoying and difficult. The best way to go about this is to make it so that we can quickly choose seeing all our habits in the day (a dashboard), then picking a habit to see it by itself to check it off the same way it is now. 

Adding a feature where after you see the piece you’ve added to your “base” by completing a habit it then transitions to the next habit in order by which you set them throughout the day.

Adding challenges and completing them gives you miniature trophies that you can view in the trophy room. The challenges can be something like keeping a constant habit streak for 20 days and you win a a trophy called ‘persistent’ that gets added to the trophy room. Then you can add trophies with tiers like the 20 day one being bronze and keeping a streak for 365 days gives you a trophy that could be called ‘unstoppable’ in the legendary or mythic tier.

Adding a rank feature that puts in different tiers based off of how many habits you have as well as how many days you’ve completed puts you in a different rank. Kinda like in the game apex; rookie, bronze, silver, gold, diamond, platinum, master, and Apex predator.

Contact me for questions or more suggestions, thank you for listening.

title: Great habit tracker, overpriced
body:
Habits is one of the best habit trackers I’ve ever used. It’s beautiful, fun, encouraging, and the satisfaction of getting another level makes it so I don’t need 50 notifications a day to open it (and it doesn’t send you a ton like other apps.)

The big problem is it’s subscription. It’s $70/year if you want any decent “skins”, the cheaper tier doesn’t include any fun ones. That’s way too much for a habits app.

Theoretically it includes 3 other apps, but this is the only good one. The other apps included are extremely over-designed and underpowered, an example of when you have designers over following trends who’ve never used the app they’re building. The calculator app is great until it lags while you type a 3 digit number, the weather app doesn’t look as good or act as well as the stock weather app that’s free or something like Carrot weather which is cheaper. The timer app has no live activity support, doesn’t support hours, and is just all around unusable. Out of all the apps, this one feels like the devs never opened a timer before in their life.

Anyway, great habits app, shouldn’t cost as much.

title: Great Concept. Poor Usability.
body:
The tone of the interface has such a fun attitude that it’s such a nice break from the mundane habit / tasks apps out there. Completing a task is such a blast.

However, once you actually try to use it, this app falls apart. Ambiguous icons without labels, unintuitive swipes that reveal different views (but also accidentally rotating the 3D trophy to no end), no consolidated list / calendar view of all of your habits, focusing the entire app experience on building a 3D model (how does this help?) etc.

It’s a shame - this is a great experimental app with some of the best micro-animations & interactions of any app. Too bad it didn’t seem to focus on what the user actually needs to do.
